haiku-low.q1: They see the generic 200 message, "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent and nothing is written.
haiku-low.q2: They get the same generic 200 response. Nothing is sent and nothing is written, since requests over 3 per hour are refused.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes. It ends sooner if a newer link is issued, if it is used or revoked, or after a successful reset.
haiku-low.q4: The link is unchanged and still works until it expires. The form is shown again with a 422, and nothing is changed.
haiku-low.q5: None. A successful reset deletes all of the user's sessions and issues no session cookie. The user logs in at /login with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: After 3 failed retries with backoff, the job is logged and dropped. No email is sent and the user is not told. The token expires unused.
haiku-low.q7: The job stores the raw token encrypted with an application key. The worker decrypts it, builds the link with PUBLIC_BASE_URL, and sends the email.
haiku-low.q8: The server SHA-256 hashes the token and looks up the row by token_hash. It is valid if used_at and revoked_at are NULL and expires_at is later than now().
haiku-low.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table, counted by user_id and created_at over the last hour. Old rows fall out of the count as their created_at passes the one-hour window.
haiku-low.q10: Unused earlier tokens are revoked at step 4, in the same transaction as the new token insert, while the account row lock is held.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: update password_hash, mark token used, revoke other tokens, delete sessions, and add the password-changed job. The confirmation email is queued in that same commit.
haiku-low.q12: The token row is locked with SELECT FOR UPDATE and rechecked. The second submit sees the token as used and gets the expired page, so one reset applies.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic 200 "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent and nothing is written.
sonnet.q2: The count of tokens issued in the last hour is already 3 or more, so it skips to commit. The user gets the same generic 200, no email is sent, and nothing is written.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = created_at + 30 min). It ends sooner if it is used, or revoked when a newer link is issued or after another reset succeeds (other tokens of the user are revoked).
sonnet.q4: Unchanged. The server returns 422 and shows the form again, the token is untouched, and the link works until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted and no session cookie is set. The user is redirected (303) to /login and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs and drops the job. No email is sent and the user is not told. The token expires unused, and the dropped email still counts toward the quota.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is encrypted with an application key and put in the email job as token_ciphertext. The worker decrypts it, builds the link {PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/reset?t=<token> and sends the email.
sonnet.q8: It computes sha256 of the token from the URL and looks for a row with that hash. The token is valid if used_at is NULL, revoked_at is NULL and expires_at > now().
sonnet.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table. The count is of token rows created in the last hour, using the (user_id, created_at) index. Rows drop out once they are older than one hour, and an hourly purge deletes rows older than 24 h.
sonnet.q10: In the request transaction, step 4, after the rate-limit check passes, the account's unused tokens are revoked and then the new token row is inserted. The old links' queued jobs are skipped by the worker.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: update users.password_hash, set the token's used_at, revoke the user's other tokens, delete all the user's sessions, and add the "password changed" job. The job is written in the same transaction, before COMMIT, so it exists only if the reset committed.
sonnet.q12: The submit takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the token row and re-checks that the token is still valid under the lock. The second submit sees a used token, rolls back, and gets the expired page.
